correctness.rationale: The two canonical kernels give an exact matching-offdiagonal-pair covariance identity; the explicit Anderson–Darling logarithmic kernel reduces the cross moment to a Bernoulli-polynomial integral, evaluated in two exact independent forms. A positive Fourier series proves all-order positivity. Strict monotonicity follows from monotone likelihood ratios of the frequency weights and a rational sample-size variance factor. The first Fourier mode yields the nonzero floor. The standalone standard-library checker passes 129 exact and diagnostic assertions, with simulations treated as non-proof.

value.rationale: The mixed finite-n covariance and exact order/sample-size correlation law quantify unavoidable shared null variation between widely used tail-weighted Anderson–Darling and recursively centered multiscale Watson goodness-of-fit diagnostics. The positive correlation floor shows that using arbitrarily high Watson integration order does not eliminate redundancy. This is a structural all-order calibration fact, not a routine restatement of separate marginal moments; a joint test would need its full distribution beyond this contribution.
